problem: GUI navigation and embodied navigation agents are trained separately with disparate data and action spaces, so they need two models, generalize poorly out-of-domain, and existing RFT methods use sparse binary grounding rewards that make GRPO inefficient.
motivation: Both tasks operate on egocentric visual observations and can be cast as MDPs, so a single policy could share grounding and spatial reasoning skills. Unifying them lowers training and deployment cost and may improve OOD generalization.
key_idea: Reformulate embodied navigation as visual-target trajectories with a click-like MOVETO(x,y) action so that GUI and embodied data share one action format, then train one policy with GRPO using a distance-aware dense grounding reward.
insight: Mixed GUI+embodied training beats single-domain training at every data scale and on all base models tested (Qwen2.5VL-3B, Qwen2VL-7B), and the 5:5 ratio is best. This indicates the two domains share transferable grounding and spatial reasoning. The dense reward yields faster-rising reward curves and better results than the sparse one, and mix single-phase training beats two-stage schedules. Depth in the reward is only for robustness: a too-strict threshold of 0.1 m hurts (Where2Place 36.84 vs 52.97).
method: Unified action space: actions split into specific (STOP, BACK), view-shifting (SCROLL up/down/left/right for GUI; TURN left/right/around/down for embodied), and localization actions (CLICK(x,y) for GUI; MOVETO(x,y) for embodied replacing MOVEFORWARD).

Visual-target embodied trajectories: take shortest-path (A*) points in Habitat/MP3D, transform the next waypoint into the current camera frame and project it to a pixel target; if it falls outside the view, insert TURN actions until visible, then emit MOVETO(x,y); end with STOP.
Reasoning thought generation: GPT-4o writes a ~60-word first-person rationale for each step (using the next screenshot for GUI), so history holds (thought, action) pairs instead of bare actions.

Unified GRPO (R1-Zero style): each step is a sample with instruction, history, observation and a depth map (zeros for 2D GUI); G=5 rollouts, group-normalized advantage, KL 0.01, EasyR1 on Qwen2.5VL-7B.
Distance-aware reward: R = 0.1*format + 1*type + 1*grounding; grounding = (1 - d/θd) if pixel distance d<θd=200 px and depth disparity <θh=1 m, else 0.
Training data: 20k samples, 10k GUI from GUI-Odyssey and 10k embodied from Matterport3D trajectories plus RoboPoint affordance data, mixed 5:5 in one phase.

setting.training_data: 20k samples: 10k GUI-Odyssey GUI trajectories + 10k embodied (Matterport3D shortest-path visual-target trajectories and RoboPoint spatial affordance data); GPT-4o-generated thoughts
setting.observation: single egocentric RGB image (GUI screenshot or embodied view) plus text history of thoughts/actions; depth used only for reward
setting.action_space: unified: click/moveto pixel coordinates, scroll/turn (left/right/around/down), long press, type, home/back, stop
setting.simulator: Habitat (Matterport3D scenes, ObjectNav via VLMNav framework); GUI offline benchmarks
setting.privileged: none at test time (depth and shortest-path GT used only for training data and reward)

numbers.extra: Run inside VLMNav framework with the agent model swapped; success threshold 0.3; the paper names only 'unseen validation of ObjectNav', so dataset version is unspecified; text says SR 33.10 but table prints 33.20

Table 'Results on embodied navigation': Ours (w/o GUI) 31.10 / 11.20

numbers_note: Only ObjectNav is a standard navigation benchmark; the dataset (HM3D vs MP3D) is not explicitly stated, so HM3D-ObjNav is a guess. GUI and spatial affordance results are not in the canonical list and are omitted. Baseline Qwen2.5VL-7B gets 27.23 SR / 9.68 SPL.
results: NaviMaster gets SR 33.20 / SPL 12.60 on ObjectNav in the VLMNav framework, vs 27.23 / 9.68 for base Qwen2.5VL-7B and 13.01 / 2.80 for RoboPoint. It also outperforms GUI RFT baselines (e.g. GUI-R1, UI-AGILE) on most OOD GUI benchmarks and beats RoboPoint-13B on all four spatial affordance benchmarks (e.g. Where2Place 52.97 vs 46.77).
limitations: Still treats GUI and embodied navigation as separate tasks; no trajectories interleave both.
Embodied evaluation is limited to ObjectNav with no prior trained baselines under VLMNav; absolute SR is low and the setup is single-view without real robot experiments.
Embodied trajectories are from shortest paths (A*), which are not human-like exploration.
